policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Both readings hold the same words in a different order; ASV 'that I myself were anathema from Christ' renders each identically in English word order and the only note is an alternative_rendering on 'could wish'. Nothing distinguishes the Greek order.
phaulon and kakon are both rendered 'bad'; ASV 'neither having done anything good or bad' fits either and no note is attached.
kathos and kathaper are synonymous comparatives; ASV 'Even as it is written' renders either, and the only note is a cross-reference to Mal. 1:2f.
The readings differ only in the position of gar and the dative spelling of Moses; ASV 'For he saith to Moses' renders both alike.
moi oun and oun moi contain the same two words; ASV 'Thou wilt say then unto me' reflects English idiom, not the Greek order, and cannot separate them.

This is a second oun in the same short sentence, in 'Ti [oun] eti memphetai'. ASV renders the connective once, in 'Thou wilt say then unto me', and the question that follows is bare: 'Why doth he still find fault?' An additional inferential particle would have surfaced as 'why then'; its absence shows the omitting reading.

ASV opens the verse with the particle and only then the address: 'Nay but, O man, who art thou'. That is the order of Menounge o anthrope; the readings placing o anthrope first would yield 'O man, nay but'.
ASV text begins 'and that he might make known', rendering kai, and the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities omit and' puts the omission in the margin rather than the text.
ASV 'in the place where it was said unto them' renders autois; the omitting reading leaves 'unto them' unaccounted for.
hypoleimma and kataleimma are both 'remnant'; ASV 'it is the remnant that shall be saved' renders either, and the only note is a cross-reference to Isa. 10:22f.
ASV ends the verse at 'finishing it and cutting it short', with no equivalent for the longer reading's added 'in righteousness, because a shortened word'.

ASV's second clause is 'did not arrive at that law', bare nomon; the expanded reading would have given 'a law of righteousness' a second time, as in the verse's first clause where ASV does print 'of righteousness'.
ASV reads 'but as it were by works', with no 'of the law'; the alternative_rendering note recasts the clause's English but likewise carries only 'by works'.
ASV starts a new sentence, 'They stumbled at the stone of stumbling', with no 'for'; the added gar would have been rendered as an inferential connective.
ASV reads 'And he that believeth on him shall not be put to shame', without the 'whosoever' that pas would supply. The alternative_rendering note offers 'it' for 'him' and does not bear on this unit.
